lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: name: codebase-design

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: description: Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: # Codebase Design

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Design **deep modules**: a lot of behaviour behind a small interface, placed at a clean seam, testable through that interface. Use this language and these principles wherever code is being designed or restructured. The aim is leverage for callers, locality for maintainers, and testability for everyone.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Glossary

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Use these terms exactly — don't substitute "component," "service," "API," or "boundary." Consistent language is the whole point.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: **Module** — anything with an interface and an implementation. Deliberately scale-agnostic: a function, class, package, or tier-spanning slice. _Avoid_: unit, component, service.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: **Interface** — everything a caller must know to use the module correctly: the type signature, but also invariants, ordering constraints, error modes, required configuration, and performance characteristics. _Avoid_: API, signature (too narrow — they refer only to the type-level surface).

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: **Implementation** — what's inside a module, its body of code. Distinct from **Adapter**: a thing can be a small adapter with a large implementation (a Postgres repo) or a large adapter with a small implementation (an in-memory fake). Reach for "adapter" when the seam is the topic; "implementation" otherwise.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: **Depth** — leverage at the interface: the amount of behaviour a caller (or test) can exercise per unit of interface they have to learn. A module is **deep** when a large amount of behaviour sits behind a small interface, **shallow** when the interface is nearly as complex as the implementation.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: **Seam** _(Michael Feathers)_ — a place where you can alter behaviour without editing in that place; the *location* at which a module's interface lives. Where to put the seam is its own design decision, distinct from what goes behind it. _Avoid_: boundary (overloaded with DDD's bounded context).

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: **Adapter** — a concrete thing that satisfies an interface at a seam. Describes *role* (what slot it fills), not substance (what's inside).

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: **Leverage** — what callers get from depth: more capability per unit of interface they learn. One implementation pays back across N call sites and M tests.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: **Locality** — what maintainers get from depth: change, bugs, knowledge, and verification concentrate in one place rather than spreading across callers. Fix once, fixed everywhere.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Deep vs shallow

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: **Deep module** = small interface + lots of implementation:

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: │   Small Interface   │  ← Few methods, simple params

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: │  Deep Implementation│  ← Complex logic hidden

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: **Shallow module** = large interface + little implementation (avoid):

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: │       Large Interface           │  ← Many methods, complex params

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: │  Thin Implementation            │  ← Just passes through

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: When designing an interface, ask:

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Can I reduce the number of methods?

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Can I simplify the parameters?

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - Can I hide more complexity inside?

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Principles

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Depth is a property of the interface, not the implementation.** A deep module can be internally composed of small, mockable, swappable parts — they just aren't part of the interface. A module can have **internal seams** (private to its implementation, used by its own tests) as well as the **external seam** at its interface.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **The deletion test.** Imagine deleting the module. If complexity vanishes, it was a pass-through. If complexity reappears across N callers, it was earning its keep.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **The interface is the test surface.** Callers and tests cross the same seam. If you want to test *past* the interface, the module is probably the wrong shape.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **One adapter means a hypothetical seam. Two adapters means a real one.** Don't introduce a seam unless something actually varies across it.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Designing for testability

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: Good interfaces make testing natural:

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 1. **Accept dependencies, don't create them.**

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ```typescript

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: // Testable

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: function processOrder(order, paymentGateway) {}

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: // Hard to test

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: function processOrder(order) {

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: const gateway = new StripeGateway();

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 2. **Return results, don't produce side effects.**

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ```typescript

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: // Testable

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: function calculateDiscount(cart): Discount {}

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: // Hard to test

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: function applyDiscount(cart): void {

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: cart.total -= discount;

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: 3. **Small surface area.** Fewer methods = fewer tests needed. Fewer params = simpler test setup.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Relationships

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - A **Module** has exactly one **Interface** (the surface it presents to callers and tests).

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Depth** is a property of a **Module**, measured against its **Interface**.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - A **Seam** is where a **Module**'s **Interface** lives.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - An **Adapter** sits at a **Seam** and satisfies the **Interface**.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Depth** produces **Leverage** for callers and **Locality** for maintainers.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Rejected framings

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Depth as ratio of implementation-lines to interface-lines** (Ousterhout): rewards padding the implementation. We use depth-as-leverage instead.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **"Interface" as the TypeScript `interface` keyword or a class's public methods**: too narrow — interface here includes every fact a caller must know.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **"Boundary"**: overloaded with DDD's bounded context. Say **seam** or **interface**.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: ## Going deeper

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Deepening a cluster given its dependencies** — see [DEEPENING.md](DEEPENING.md): dependency categories, seam discipline, and replace-don't-layer testing.

lines.author: matemolnar8
lines.text: - **Exploring alternative interfaces** — see [DESIGN-IT-TWICE.md](DESIGN-IT-TWICE.md): spin up parallel sub-agents to design the interface several radically different ways, then compare on depth, locality, and seam placement.
